topPRs.title: feat: enforce review period delay ranges and lockbox consistency
topPRs.author: 0xarktos
topPRs.body:
## Description

Adds validation for the per-chain review period delays (proof maturity, dispute game finality and DelayedWETH delay) introduced in ethereum-optimism/optimism#23215 and ethereum-optimism/optimism#23215

The standard ranges for these delays are widened to the configured bounds and a range is added for the DelayedWETH delay. The staging compliance report now shows the delays of a new chain against those ranges, and a new check groups every registered chain by `ETHLockbox` and asserts that the delays are within range and identical across chains sharing a lockbox, including those in the interop set.

## Changes

- `validation`: `proof_maturity_delay_seconds` is `[86400, 604800]`, `dispute_game_finality_delay_seconds` is `[43200, 302400]`, and a new `[delayed_weth] delay_seconds = [43200, 604800]` table and `DelayedWETHParams` struct are added. The bounds match `op-deployer`'s `standard` package and `StandardValidatorUtils.sol`. `Range.WithinRange`, previously unused, get a test.
- `ops/internal/report`: `ScanL1` reads the three delays via a new `ScanReviewPeriod` and the comment template renders a "Review Period Delays" block. Both delays are read from the OptimismPortal, which keeps a legacy `disputeGameFinalityDelaySeconds()` forwarding to the AnchorStateRegistry on every release, so no release gating is needed. `checkmarkRangeUint64` now delegates to `Range.WithinRange` instead of reimplementing it.
- `ops/internal/manage`: `ReviewPeriodChecker` reads the delays of every chain with an `EthLockboxProxy` over the superchain's L1 RPC and fails on out-of-range values or on any difference between chains sharing a lockbox. All three delays are compared, matching `OPContractsManagerMigrator._validateSharedDelays`. The DelayedWETH is resolved from `SystemConfig.delayedWETH()` because `addresses.json` has no `DelayedWETHProxy` for permissioned-only chains.
- `ops/cmd/check_review_period_delays`, a `just check-review-period-delays` recipe, a `check-review-period-delays` CircleCI job on PRs and a copy in the daily scheduled workflow, since delays change through superchain-ops tasks rather than registry PRs.

## Notes

- Today all 8 lockbox chains are on distinct lockboxes with the default delays, so the equality rule is vacuous until interop sets share a lockbox. Verified against the live registry.
- The lockbox check is also run by `TestReviewPeriodChecker_actual` inside the existing `go-lint-test-ops` job, so the dedicated CI job only adds the daily run.

Closes [#812](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism-private/issues/812)

topPRs.title: feat(ops): add read-only check of chain TOML roles/addresses against onchain state
topPRs.author: OptimismBot
topPRs.body:
## Problem

Nothing checks that the hand-maintained `[roles]` and `[addresses]` in `superchain/configs/<superchain>/<chain>.toml` still match the chain's actual onchain state. The daily-codegen job fetches onchain data, but it only writes `superchain/extra/addresses/addresses.json` and `chainList.*`. When the two disagree, nothing fails.

Example: Unichain's L1 ProxyAdmin owner changed onchain on 2026-09-13 from `0x6d5B183F538ABB8572F5cD17109c617b994D5833` to `0x5a0Aae59D09fccBdDb6C6CcEB07B7279367C3d2A`. Daily codegen picked up the new owner in `addresses.json` (#1335). `superchain/configs/mainnet/unichain.toml` still has the old owner, and no check caught it.

## Design

- New tool `ops/cmd/check_onchain_configs`. It uses the same path as codegen to fetch data: `manage.FetchChains` (op-fetcher) and then `config.CreateAddressesWithRolesFromFetcher`. It then compares each chain's TOML against that data with `manage.DiffChainAgainstOnchain`.
- The tool only reads. It never writes TOML or any other file.
- It compares only fields that are present in the TOML, in both `[roles]` and `[addresses]`. Many configs list only some fields (for example, most list only `ProxyAdminOwner` under `[roles]`), and missing fields are skipped.
- Each mismatch prints one line per chain and field, for example:
  `[NOTOK] mainnet/unichain (chain 130): [roles] ProxyAdminOwner: toml=0x6d5B… onchain=0x5a0A…`
  The tool exits non-zero if any chain has a mismatch.
- If the fetcher returns the zero address for a field the TOML sets, the tool prints `[ WARN]` and does not fail. A zero address means the fetcher could not find the field, not that the TOML is wrong. Today this happens with `DisputeGameFactoryProxy` on several chains whose fault-proof wiring the fetcher doesn't detect.
- CI: the new `check-onchain-configs` job runs in the scheduled `daily-codegen` workflow. It runs alongside codegen, uses the same contexts and RPC secrets, and sends a Slack alert to `#notify-ci` and @protocol-oncall on failure, the same way `daily-codegen` does. I did not add it to per-PR CI. Onchain state changes without any PR, and right now the check would fail every PR (see below). Once the existing mismatches are fixed, it can also go into the `main` workflow.
- You can run it locally with `just check-onchain-configs <sepolia_rpc>,<mainnet_rpc>`. It also accepts `--chain-ids` and `--superchains`.

## Current state on main: this check will fail

I ran the check against public RPCs (publicnode). It reports 14 chains that disagree with onchain state, including mainnet/unichain. A separate PR fixes `unichain.toml`. The other chains need their own fixes, so this job will fail until all of them are updated. I spot-checked a few results by calling `owner()` directly on the ProxyAdmin. The onchain values also match what `addresses.json` already has.

| chain | field | toml | onchain |
|---|---|---|---|
| mainnet/unichain (130) | ProxyAdminOwner | 0x6d5B183F538ABB8572F5cD17109c617b994D5833 | 0x5a0Aae59D09fccBdDb6C6CcEB07B7279367C3d2A |
| mainnet/hashkeychain (177) | ProxyAdminOwner | 0x441F31C4cdf772558D4EA31f3114de59aE145E7c | 0x3228F00FbFD0e1F4c282601c489664B10932C40f |
| mainnet/metal (1750) | ProxyAdminOwner | 0x5a0Aae59D09fccBdDb6C6CcEB07B7279367C3d2A | 0x4a4962275DF8C60a80d3a25faEc5AA7De116A746 |
| mainnet/mint (185) | ProxyAdminOwner | 0x4a4962275DF8C60a80d3a25faEc5AA7De116A746 | 0x3c54Be307E15258E51d42E585831bD7E04BBc03b |
| mainnet/mode (34443) | ProxyAdminOwner | 0x5a0Aae59D09fccBdDb6C6CcEB07B7279367C3d2A | 0x4a4962275DF8C60a80d3a25faEc5AA7De116A746 |

Warnings only (`DisputeGameFactoryProxy` is set in the TOML, but the fetcher returned the zero address): mainnet automata, ethernity, redstone, swan, tbn, xterio-eth; sepolia camp, cyber, funki, lisk, ozean, pivotal, tbn.

## Testing

- `go build ./...`, `go vet`, and `golangci-lint` (v1.64.8) pass on the changed packages in `ops`. The `go test ./internal/manage/ ./internal/config/` tests pass, including the new `TestDiffChainAgainstOnchain`.
- I ran `go run ./cmd/check_onchain_configs` against public Sepolia and mainnet RPCs. It produced the results above, and `--chain-ids` filtering works.
- I have not run the new CircleCI job. It will first run on the next `build_daily` schedule or a `daily_codegen_dispatch` trigger.

topPRs.title: ops: keep genesis files as opaque JSON
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
Stacked on #1382 (needs its monorepo bump for `op-core/genesis`).

The registry no longer uses op-geth's genesis types: it keeps genesis files as opaque JSON, validates them with op-core, and writes op-deployer's genesis as is. Decoding through `core.Genesis` keeps only the fields the linked geth knows, and upstream go-ethereum's chain config has no OP fields (`optimism`, `regolithTime`…`jovianTime`, `bedrockBlock`), so on upstream geth these would be dropped silently from every genesis the registry publishes.

- `ReadGenesis`/`WriteGenesis` (used by `sync_staging`) keep the genesis JSON byte for byte. `TestGenesisRoundTrip` round-trips every file under `superchain/extra/genesis` and checks the bytes are unchanged; some files are pretty-printed, so a decode and re-encode would not keep them.
- `ValidateGenesisIntegrity` builds an `op-core/params.ChainConfig` from the chain's TOML and compares `op-core/genesis.ToBlock().Hash()` instead of hand-building an op-geth config. Every chain `check_genesis_integrity` checks still matches its hash. op-core rejects `stateHash`, which only the legacy-migrated chains the check already skips use.
- `create_config` writes `op-deployer inspect genesis` output compacted, which keeps its key order (go-ethereum's `core.Genesis` order). This drops `opaqueToGenesis` and its losslessness check. Unlike before, an old op-deployer's `terminalTotalDifficultyPassed` is kept and op-geth's `"slotNumber":null` is no longer added.

topPRs.title: feat: add GIWA Sepolia Testnet
topPRs.author: ZakAyesh
topPRs.body:
Lands #1368 from an internal branch. That PR comes from an organization fork, which cannot grant maintainer edit access and does not get CI secrets, so it cannot be finished in place. The first commit here is @ihooni's original commit unchanged; the second is the maintainer steps from docs/ops.md.

## Chain

GIWA Sepolia Testnet, chain ID 91342, OP Enterprise self-managed. See #1368 for the operator's full write-up. Summary of what was verified on chain and on explorers:

- Deployment tx [`0xf4b05ce5…1240`](https://eth-sepolia.blockscout.com/tx/0xf4b05ce502142616c0d7d533348ca18d77fc832f090c870ecf347a889a921240) in block 8830872 via OPCM `0xEbBAD33C…` created the four proxies in `[addresses]`.
- `ProxyAdminOwner` `0x0B266965c88C78f17e1F9f59784249bf8Da1CB9E` is a 2-of-2 Safe v1.3.0 and owns `ProxyAdmin` `0x6AdB900DC56F7028D5E7943638897C8103cf0da5`, so `governed_by_optimism = false`.
- Custom `SuperchainConfig` `0xEF3a8c9Ec7873C3ACEE4e6153fb66072cdE9032d` (deployed with `configType = "custom"`).
- Every field in the generated `giwa.toml` matches the operator's published [rollup config](https://github.com/giwa-io/node/blob/main/genesis/consensus/sepolia-rollup.json): genesis L1/L2 hashes and numbers, `l2_time`, system config, block/sequencer params, all hardfork times, batch inbox, portal and system config addresses, EIP-1559 params.
- `keep_karst_upgrade_gas` stays unset (false): the Karst activation block carried a one-off gas limit and the next block returned to 60M.

## Short name

Staged as `giwasepolia` to match ethereum-lists (required by `check-chainlist`, which passed before the rename), then renamed to `giwa` at the operator's request so the identifier is `sepolia/giwa` and the network name `giwa-sepolia`. Same pattern as `arena-z-testnet` → `arena-z` in #1092.

## Unrelated hunks in addresses.json

Codegen for the sepolia superchain also picked up role drift on Unichain Sepolia (1301): `BatchSubmitter`, `Proposer`, `UnsafeBlockSigner`. These hunks are byte-identical to #1369. They cannot be dropped from this PR because `check-codegen` regenerates the whole superchain and fails on any drift. Whichever PR lands first, the other merges cleanly.

## Checks run locally

- `just check-chainlist` (pre-rename: passed; post-rename: no staged config, as CI will see it)
- `just sync-staging --l1-rpc-urls=$SEPOLIA_RPC_URL`
- `just codegen $SEPOLIA_RPC_URL sepolia`
- `just check-genesis-integrity` (sepolia/giwa OK)
- `just apply-hardforks` (no diff)
- `check_depsets` (55 chains processed)
- `sync_staging` re-run on the empty staging dir (no diff)

topPRs.title: ops: bump monorepo to develop and switch to op-service/log
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
Bumps `ops` to monorepo develop at ethereum-optimism/optimism@fbfb3587c9 (ethereum-optimism/optimism#23527) and op-geth to `v1.101702.4-rc.1`, the version that commit pins.

- ethereum-optimism/optimism#23527 moved op-fetcher's library: the `fetch/script` types are now in `op-fetcher/chaininfo` (`ChainConfig` → `Config`, `CreateChainConfig(out)` → `out.Config()`), with the same JSON shape. op-fetcher now reads chain info with `eth_call`s instead of a forge script. A full `codegen` run against public L1 RPCs gives the same output on this branch as on `main`.
- `fetch.NewFetcher` now takes `op-service/log`'s `Logger`, so `ops` logs through `op-service/log` instead of `go-ethereum/log`.
- The `validation` requirement in `ops/go.mod` moves up to the version the monorepo requires. `ops/go.work` still resolves it to the local module.
